overnightRisk: This is the widest gap of the week: the next report is at 02:00 COT but the next liquid session is Monday, so the book is exposed for roughly forty-eight hours with no ETF creations, no US equity tape and no macro print to anchor price. Six specific catalysts. ONE - Friday's ETF flow is UNKNOWN. The Farside 04 September row was still all dashes at 19:35 COT, so the +730.8m that bought Thursday's rally has no Friday counterpart yet; if it prints negative it will print into a weekend book with nobody there to absorb it. TWO - positioning is crowded long and getting more so. The long/short account ratio is 1.05, realised long liquidations run 3.21:1 over shorts, and open interest is still bleeding (-19,526,481 USD since midday, on top of -142,698,779 in the prior leg). Falling OI with a crowded long book means the remaining longs are the stubborn ones, and stubborn longs are what a weekend flush is for. THREE - the largest single liquidation pocket on the entire map, 2,210,857 USD with 1,787,993 of it long, sits just 156.8 points BELOW spot at 79,500, and below that a 100 percent long 1,632,479 USD pocket at 78,750. Thin weekend books plus a magnet that close is the classic setup for a wick that would never happen on a Tuesday. FOUR - volatility is compressed to a spring. The 15-minute ATR collapsed 56.4 percent to 122.14 and the hourly fell 26.8 percent to 459.18; price is pinned in a 45-point sandwich between the 15m EMA200 at 79,637.34 below and the 15m EMA20 at 79,682.37 above. Compression of this order resolves with an expansion, and the direction is not knowable in advance. FIVE - the daily MACD histogram just crossed negative for the first time in the advance while daily RSI is still 66.49, so the momentum unwind has room to run without the trend technically breaking. SIX - macro is a mild headwind into the close: DXY finished +0.25 percent at 99.157 and the US 10-year rose 2.2 basis points to 4.784 percent, both firmer dollar and firmer rates. The protection is a resting stop at 78,950 on the long book and a small 30 USD futures hedge stopped at 80,250; neither will help against a gap THROUGH those levels, which is the residual risk that cannot be removed in a paper book.

calibration.note: A quiet, correct session for the framework and a small win for the discretionary side. Neither midday gate fired and both refusals were right. The 78,330.0 reduce sat 1,128.2 points under spot when it was written and price never came within 1,046.4 points of it - a gate that wide is only defensible because the hourly ATR had just expanded 32.6 percent, and the ATR has since contracted 26.8 percent, which is exactly why this report pulls the reduce gate up to 79,150. The 79,900.0 add gate is the more instructive one: the session high was 79,869.6, thirty points and thirty cents short, and that hour closed 79,704.2. A settled-close gate placed 0.5 hourly ATRs beyond a proven wick refused to arm on a touch for the third consecutive session, which is now a pattern rather than luck. The midday's watch item resolved BULLISH - the 79,624 confluence was reclaimed on five straight hourly closes - and the midday's second watch item, the Friday ETF row, is STILL UNRESOLVED because Farside has not published it. The discretionary side won small: the midday ADD bought 10 USDT of spot at 79,458.2 which now marks 79,656.8, +0.25 percent, roughly +0.025 USDT on the size. The honest scale of that is a rounding error; the meaningful part is that the session did not need to act again.
